thread.title: Some Ways To Play The E-Commerce Boom

author: Matt Bohlsen
title: Some Ways To Play The E-Commerce Boom
text:
Note: All data is as of April 26, when this article was first published.
E-commerce is defined as "the activity of buying or selling of products and services online or over the internet." E-commerce or more simply "online shopping/business" is becoming increasingly common with growth rates of ~20% globally, higher in ASEAN countries.
The e-commerce trend E-commerce growth forecasts
The graph below from eMarketer forecast retail e-commerce sales will increase to $4.058 trillion in 2020, making up 14.6% of total retail spending that year. More significantly growth rates around 20% pa are to be expected.
Source
Note: ASEAN e-commerce spending is forecast to grow at a 32% CAGR and rising to almost US$90b by 2025. The chart below shows a forecast 8.8 fold increase in the next 8 years for the SE Asia e-commerce market.
Southeast Asia's set for explosive e-commerce growth
Source
Note: The e-commerce "logistics" growth forecast is a CAGR of 19.5%.
Asia Pacific is leading the world in [Business to Consumer] B2C e-commerce as a percentage of sales
Source : yStats.com
We can see from the graph above that in 2016 e-commerce as a percentage of total retail sales is still mostly under 10%, with Asia-Pacific being the exception at 12.1%. This would suggest plenty of room to gain further market share.
E-commerce tailwinds
Increasing global internet penetration (currently ~50%). Increasing acceptance to use online shopping sites. A growing global middle class - most growth is in Asia or as DBS says: "Come 2020, Asia will be home to half the world's middle class."

A look at some of the main e-commerce stocks
Source: Not updated (most figures are based on 2015)
Market cap of top 12 global internet companies as of May 2017 ($b)
Source : Statista
We can see from the charts above that 6 global internet giants have the largest market caps. These six companies dominate the internet and online sales - Apple, Alphabet (Google), Amazon, Facebook, Tencent and Alibaba.
Some popular global e-commerce companies
Amazon ( AMZN ) - Price = USD 1,488
Amazon is the clear leader in the e-commerce space. In 2017 Amazon grew revenues by 30.8% to US$177b, and grew profits by 30.9% to US$2.32b. Whilst Amazon has made their name from online selling, the company has diversified using their strong brand name and is now growing very strongly in cloud storage (Amazon Web Services) and subscription services (Amazon Prime etc). Amazon's strength is their ability to disrupt other industries, rapidly gain market share, then monetize their customer base. Very few companies have had such spectacular success at growing online revenues.
Certainly the stock never comes cheap. 2018 PE is 178 , 2019 PE is 97, and 2020 PE is 55. 2018 net profit margin is a very thin 1.77% , but is forecast to increase to 3.91% by 2020. Analyst consensus estimates are an outperform rating with a target price of USD 1,657 , representing 13% upside.
Source :4-traders
Netflix ( NFLX ) - Price = USD 309
Netflix specializes in and provides streaming media and video-on-demand online. In 2013, Netflix expanded into film and television production as well as online distribution. Netflix has managed to completely disrupt the cable TV industry with spectacular growth in subscriber numbers now exceeding cable TV . In the first quarter of 2018, Netflix had 125 million streaming subscribers worldwide. Of these subscribers, 56.71 million were from the United States.
Source
2018 PE is 36 and 2019 PE is 28. 2018 net profit margin is 23.82%. Analyst consensus estimates are an outperform rating with a target price of USD 330 , representing 8% upside.
Tencent [HK:0700] [GR:NNND] ( OTCPK:TCEHY ) - Price = HKD 382, USD 48.75
Tencent is the Facebook of China and more. Tencent is China's social media and gaming giant owning WeChat, QQ.com and Tencent QQ. The company also has interests in many other e-commerce companies including JD.com , Sea, Go-Jek, Traveloka, Pomelo Fashion and Tiki.vn ; as well as interest in the areas of cloud, AI, robotics, virtual reality, music, real estate, financial services, and automotive.
Wikipedia states :
Tencent is the world's biggest investment corporation, one of the largest Internet and technology companies, as well as the largest and most valuable gaming ( Tencent Games ) and social media company in the world. Its many services include social network , music , web portals , e-commerce , mobile games , internet services , payment systems , smartphones , and multiplayer online games , which are all among the world's biggest and most successful in their respective categories.
2018 PE is 36 and 2019 PE is 28. 2018 net profit margin is 23.82%. Analyst consensus estimates are an outperform rating with a target price of CNY 419 , representing 34% upside.
Source : 4-traders
Alibaba ( BABA ) - Price = USD 172
Alibaba is China's number 1 e-commerce site. Alibaba recently increased it's investment in SE Asian e-commerce giant Lazada upping its share from 51% to 83%. They also bought into Tokopedia in Indonesia. This means Alibaba have a clear growth strategy particularly in China and South Asia. They also continue to expand their offerings including Alibaba Cloud .
Alibaba has a 2018 PE of 44 and 2019 PE of 35; with 2018 net profit margins forecast at 25.95% . Analyst consensus is an outperform rating and a target price of CNY 1,394 representing 29% upside.
I recommended the stock before back in March 2016 at USD 71.33, and still see the stock as an accumulate despite quite high earnings multiples. My reason for this is that I believe their South Asian growth strategy will pay off big time with massive revenue growth due to "explosive" e-commerce growth in SE Asia (forecast to increase 8.8 fold in the next 8 years). Margins are also excellent. Looking at the chart below analysts tend to think the same.
Source : 4-traders
JD.Com ( JD ) - Price = USD 36.15
JD.Com is China's number 2 online retailer and a strong competitor to Alibaba (number 1). As of September 2017, the platform has 266.3 million active users. The main difference between the two is that Alibaba operate's a marketplace approach with its e-commerce businesses, whereas JD.com opted for an Amazon-like vertical approach. This means JD.Com has spent large amounts of CapEx focusing on warehousing and logistics as well as real world stores. This vertically integrated approach should hopefully pay off in the longer term with better margins.
JD has a 2018 PE of 121 and 2019 PE of 46; with 2018 net profit margins forecast at a mere 0.5% . Analyst consensus is an outperform rating and a target price of CNY 323 representing 42% upside.
Source : 4-traders
Shopify Inc [TSX:SHOP] ( SHOP ) - Price = USD 121.57
Shopify owns the Shopify e-commerce cloud based platform, which helps merchants sell their products and receive payments with a seamless connection. Its software is used by merchants to run business across all sales channels, including web, tablet and mobile storefronts, social media storefronts, and brick-and-mortar and pop-up shops.
The company revenues come from merchant and subscription solutions, mostly for small and medium-sized businesses. The company already has over 400,000 merchants using Shopify, and is rapidly growing revenues as you can see in the chart below. The company is forecast to be EPS positive in 2020. Analyst consensus target price is USD 145 , representing 21% upside.
Source : 4-traders
Baozun Inc. ( BZUN ) - Price =USD 44.01
Baozun is the Shopify of China as it also targets the merchants business. Baozun provide end-to-end services, including website design, development and hosting, IT infrastructure, customer service, warehousing and logistics services, as well as digital marketing.
Also like Shopify revenues have been rising very rapidly to the point where the company is already profitable. 2018 PE is 39 , and 2019 PE is 25. 2018 net profit margin is 7.78% . Analyst consensus target price is CNY 288 representing 4.6% upside.
Source : 4-traders
Further reading 10 Ecommerce Trends That Will Shape Southeast Asian Ecommerce in 2018 Global Investment Trends To Grow Your Wealth - 'The Rising Asian Middle Class' 3 Ways To Play The Rising Asian Middle Class | Seeking Alpha Note: I did not discuss Facebook ( FB ), Alphabet Google ( GOOGL ) ( GOOG ) and Apple ( AAPL ) here as they are well known internet stocks. The first two earn mostly from online advertising, while Apple mostly earns from smartphones and other electronics (increasingly from Apple online services). Also I did not discuss eBay or PayPal as I don't see them growing nearly as well as the other companies discussed. Finally India's Flipkart has potential but is not easily accessible to investors, although this may soon change if Walmart ( WMT ) buys Flipkart.
Conclusion E-commerce is a very significant trend this decade that was born from the internet boom. Growth is forecast to increase at ~20%pa, and even higher in the Asia Pacific region due to the rising Asian middle class.
There are many ways to invest in this boom, and choosing the best way is the challenge. My view is that investors should look to take some core positions in the major global players such as the FANG stocks (Facebook, Amazon, Netflix and Google) which have recently shed about $100b in value this past week, allowing a nice entry point. These stocks have huge global reach, strong brand names, and quite strong moats. Some would even suggest Apple be added to this elite group due to their online services.
However, most of the next decades growth in e-commerce will be driven by the rising global middle class most of whom are in Asia. This will mean investors should consider some exposure to the key Asian e-commerce giants such as the Alibaba, Tencent, and JD.com (I call them the JAT stocks).
Some smaller growing online companies such as Netflix, Shopify, Bauzon also have good potential.
My approach will be to look to accumulate some more of the FANG and JAT stocks on weakness. For buying now my preferred e-commerce picks would be Alibaba and Tencent.
To be clear the FANG and JAT stocks are all very high quality superb growth stocks. They don't come cheap so they are definitely on my buy list for the next major market downturn.
As usual, all comments are welcome.
